topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces complement as a challenging but essential topic in immunology.

topics.label: Principles, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall framework of the complement system, its naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream pathways that converge to trigger surface-bound C3 convertase activity.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and recruits immune cells.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the specific disease phenotypes and diagnostic patterns associated with deficiencies in individual complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary mechanisms used by pathogens to subvert and survive complement attack.

topics.label: Conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture topic.
